routing_warnings.description: The client expresses uncertainty about attaining acceptable animation quality and conditions further testing or investment on confidence in that quality; the message does not clearly change animation's status as the preferred primary medium.
The consistency instruction applies specifically to newly generated set images rather than character styling.
The preferred reference is selected for its character details and features, making detail fidelity the narrower target.
The client withdraws the freelancer's one-off restyling task by deciding to perform it independently; this does not remove the desired character style.
The reported drift and requested raw graffiti aesthetic concern the character visual-style Requirement rather than character detail fidelity.
The client withdraws the freelancer's three-character restyle task by deciding to attempt it independently; this does not remove the character-detail fidelity Requirement.
The uncertainty about further animation testing and attainable animation quality belongs to the animation-quality Requirement.
The condition that new sets remain stylistically on point and consistent belongs to set-style continuity rather than set-image quality.
The statement primarily addresses whether the resulting sets remain different despite looking similar.
The client reports that the revised sets are more similar to one another, which is a distinctness failure rather than a general image-quality failure.
The missing shadows concern the independently defined character-shadow behavior.
The client's uncertainty concerns achievable animation quality and further animation testing, not set-image quality.
The client's general statement that the latest images look much better does not specifically verify visual distinctness and is better aligned with overall set-image quality.
The separate request to retain the opening long/wide shots concerns framing progression rather than set-style continuity.
The complaint that the revised sets look more similar concerns visual distinctness, not stylistic continuity.
The statement that the latest images look much better supports general image quality but does not specifically verify cross-shot style continuity.
The reported style drift and requested raw-graffiti treatment explicitly concern the three characters rather than the sets.
The separate observation that character shadows are missing belongs to the Character Shadow Rendering Requirement.
The authorization to continue SQ4 work is specifically limited to the independently modeled energy-blast treatment.
This uncertainty explicitly concerns SQ11 and SQ12 rather than the target SQ4 shot specifications.
